title: Perfect-source tensor evaluation on K-flat and K-injective representatives
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $M,F,J,I$ be cochain complexes of ordinary $R$-modules, viewed on the one-object ringed site. Use the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the product total Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], and localization $Q$ into the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume $QM$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, $F$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $J,I$ are K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $q:F\otimes_R J\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The formula on homogeneous tensors
$$t_{M,F,J,q}(f\otimes h)(x)=q(f\otimes h(x))$$
defines a chain map
$$F\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(M,J)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(M,I)$$
whose localization is an isomorphism in $D(R)$:
$$Q(F\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(M,J))\xrightarrow[Q(t_{M,F,J,q})]{\sim}Q\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(M,I).$$
Equivalently, the specified chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. Under the K-flat tensor and K-injective Hom identifications [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], this is precisely the canonical derived evaluation comparison
$$QF\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QM,QJ)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QM,QF\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QJ),$$
with $Qq$ identifying the right-hand coefficient object with $QI$. No boundedness of $F,J,I,M$, termwise projectivity of $M$, or Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is required beyond perfectness of $QM$.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), case (1); explicit projective-source comparison of K-flat/K-injective models.

proof.text:
Write $H(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(A,B)$. First form $c_M:F\otimes H(M,J)\to H(M,F\otimes J)$ by $c_M(f\otimes h)(x)=f\otimes h(x)$, and set $t_M=H(M,q)c_M$. The formula is balanced and extends over the direct sum: a homogeneous tensor is a finite sum, while each $h$ is a family in the Hom product. For $|f|=p,|h|=r$ the Hom differential of $c_M(f\otimes h)$ is the family
$$d_Ff\otimes h(x)+(-1)^pf\otimes d_Jh(x)-(-1)^{p+r}f\otimes h(d_Mx).$$
This equals $c_M(d_Ff\otimes h+(-1)^pf\otimes(d_Jh-(-1)^rh d_M))(x)$. Thus $c_M$, and then $t_M$ since $q$ is a chain map, are chain maps. No interchange of two homogeneous factors occurs, so no extra Koszul sign appears.

source.place: Tag 0BYM, lemma-diagonal-better, explicit construction and differential calculation; Tag 0BYN, lemma-internal-hom-diagonal-better

proof.text: By perfectness choose a bounded finite-projective complex $P$ and an isomorphism $QP\cong QM$. The projective-source morphism theorem represents this isomorphism by a chain map $a:P\to M$, since $P$ is bounded above and termwise projective. This $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism: each cohomology functor factors through $Q$, so $H^i(a)$ is an isomorphism. For $V=J,I$, apply K-injective Hom invariance with target map $1_V$ and source map $a$ to obtain quasi-isomorphisms $a_V^*:H(M,V)\to H(P,V)$.

source.place: Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism (1), finite-projective representative; Derived Categories Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex; Sites Cohomology Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined

proof.text:
We check $c_P$ is degreewise invertible. Let $S=\{a,\ldots,b\}$ contain the support of $P$. In degree $n$ its source and target, respectively, identify with
$$\bigoplus_p\bigoplus_{s\in S}F^p\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(P^s,J^{s+n-p}),\qquad
\bigoplus_{s\in S}\operatorname{Hom}(P^s,\bigoplus_pF^p\otimes J^{s+n-p}).$$
Finite products equal finite sums here. Tensor commutes with sums by the bilinear universal property: an inverse to the canonical comparison sends $f\otimes(y_p)_p$ to the finite sum of $f\otimes y_p$. For a finitely generated module $E$, $\operatorname{Hom}(E,\bigoplus_pN_p)=\bigoplus_p\operatorname{Hom}(E,N_p)$: the images of a finite generating set have a finite union of supports, which contains the image of every element; uniqueness is checked by projections. Apply this with $E=P^s$. After these rearrangements $c_P^n$ is the direct sum over $(p,s)$ of the finite-projective equivalences $F^p\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(P^s,J^{s+n-p})\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P^s,F^p\otimes J^{s+n-p})$, with their stated formula $f\otimes h\mapsto(x\mapsto f\otimes h(x))$. Therefore the specified $c_P$ is an isomorphism of complexes, using its chain-map property from step 1.

source.place: Tag 0BYM, lemma-diagonal-better; Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism (1), bounded finite-projective calculation

proof.text: The projective-source derived-Hom comparison is natural in the target and applies to $P$ and the arbitrary complexes $F\otimes J$ and $I$. Hence the localization of $H(P,q)$ identifies with $R\operatorname{Hom}(QP,Qq)$, which is an isomorphism. Applying cohomology through $Q$ shows that $H(P,q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Combined with step 3 this proves $t_P=H(P,q)c_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Precomposition gives a square with upper row $t_M$, lower row $t_P$, left vertical map $1_F\otimes a_J^*$ and right vertical map $a_I^*$. Both paths send $f\otimes h$ to the family $x\mapsto q(f\otimes h(a(x)))$, so the square commutes as chain maps. The two maps $a_J^*,a_I^*$ are quasi-isomorphisms by step 2, and tensoring $a_J^*$ with $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by K-flatness. The bottom row is a quasi-isomorphism by step 4. On each cohomology group, the square expresses the top map as a composite of the bottom isomorphism and the vertical isomorphisms and their inverses. Thus $t_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and its localization is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0BYM, lemma-diagonal-better, functoriality; Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism (1), source-representative comparison

proof.text:
It remains to identify the actual localized arrow with the canonical derived comparison. For source $P$, its terms are projective and hence flat, so the bounded-flat theorem makes $P$ K-flat. Put $U=F\otimes H(P,J)$. The one-K-flat uncurrying theorem applies to $(U,P,I)$, without requiring $U$ to be K-flat. The ordinary transpose of $t_P$ is
$$(F\otimes H(P,J))\otimes P\longrightarrow I,\quad(f\otimes h)\otimes x\longmapsto q(f\otimes h(x)).$$
The same uncurrying theorem applied to $(H(P,J),P,J)$ and its identity map identifies $h\otimes x\mapsto h(x)$ with the derived-Hom counit. The K-flat tensor model for $F$ identifies $Q(F\otimes J)$ with $QF\otimes^{\mathbf L}QJ$ and $QU$ with $QF\otimes^{\mathbf L}QH(P,J)$; we take these identifications, like $c_{U,P}$ and $c_{H(P,J),P}$ of the uncurrying theorem, to be the natural inverse-tensorator comparisons of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], which exist because $F$, respectively $P$, is K-flat. At chain level the transpose factors as $(F\otimes H(P,J))\otimes P\xrightarrow{\alpha}F\otimes(H(P,J)\otimes P)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}F\otimes J\xrightarrow{q}I$, where $\alpha$ is the native complex associator, given on pure generators by $(f\otimes h)\otimes x\mapsto f\otimes(h\otimes x)$ [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints], and $\mathrm{ev}(h\otimes x)=h(x)$. Since these comparisons preserve the native associator and are natural in each variable [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], writing $\alpha^{\mathbf L}$ for the derived associator and $H=H(P,J)$,
$$Q\bigl(q(1\otimes\mathrm{ev})\alpha\bigr)c_{U,P}^{-1}=Q(q)\,c_{F,J}^{-1}\,\bigl(1_{QF}\otimes Q(\mathrm{ev})c_{H,P}^{-1}\bigr)\,\alpha^{\mathbf L}\,(c_{F,H}\otimes1_{QP}).$$ Under these comparisons, the displayed transpose is therefore exactly $1_{QF}$ tensor the counit, followed by $Qq$. The uncurrying theorem therefore identifies $Q(t_P)$ with the specified derived evaluation comparison followed by $R\operatorname{Hom}(QP,Qq)$.

source.place: Tag 0BYN, lemma-internal-hom-diagonal-better, defining K-flat/K-injective model; Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective

proof.text: The K-injective models give $QH(M,J)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}(QM,QJ)$ and $QH(M,I)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}(QM,QI)$. The K-flat model for $F$, normalized as the inverse-tensorator comparison $c_{F,H(M,J)}$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] (the same normalization as in step 6), gives the required tensor identification on the source; by naturality of that comparison in its second variable it carries $1_F\otimes a_J^*$ to $1_{QF}\otimes Q(a_J^*)$. These identifications carry the vertical maps of step 5 to derived-Hom precomposition by $Qa$. For completeness, the canonical derived comparison is contravariantly natural in its Hom-source: by naturality of the tensor-Hom adjunction, precomposing either its source $H(M,J)$ or its target $H(M,F\otimes^{\mathbf L}J)$ by $a$ has transpose $F\otimes H(M,J)\otimes P\xrightarrow{1\otimes1\otimes a}F\otimes H(M,J)\otimes M\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon}F\otimes J$. Thus the derived square is the localized square of step 5. Since its vertical arrows are invertible and its bottom arrow is the canonical comparison by step 6, its top arrow $Q(t_M)$ is exactly the canonical comparison as well, with $Qq$ on the coefficient object. This proves every asserted identification, in addition to invertibility.
